title: Trust Recovery
concept: Using the Proof Protocol for a real breach of trust: name what happened, decide what needs to change, set a time window, track the facts, then check in.
whenToUse: After a betrayal, deception, repeated broken agreements, or any clear before/after change in how safe things feel.
steps: Name what happened, clearly, without deflecting.
Decide on one specific, observable change.
Set a real time window, with dates to check in.
Track it with a simple table — just the facts.
Check in — look at the record first, then talk about how it feels. Extend, adjust, or close it out.
If it's not safe, stop and get outside support.

phrases.text: What happened was ___. I'm not debating that.
My proof: ___. You'll see it when ___.

working: Named what happened. Proof: gives a heads-up if running late, plus an open calendar. Checked in weekly for 4 weeks. One partial week, owned honestly. Things feel calmer, so the window gets extended.
notWorking: Long apology speeches with no actual behavior behind them — or pushing for “trust me again” before there's any evidence — or using the tracking to shame someone.
activity: Fill in one row of proof and a 4-week table together. Use it alongside the Proof Protocol card.
warn: If it's not safe, stop and get outside support.
